historical_evidence.title: Marriage i. The Marriage Contract in the Pre-Islamic Period ii. Sogdian marriage contract.
historical_evidence.locator: Nov. 3 lines 11-17; Nov. 4 lines 7-15; discussion dating the contract to ca. 709-710 CE and probably Samarkand

spatial_interpretation.probable_context: Yakubovich states that the agreement was likely concluded in Samarkand.
spatial_interpretation.document_findspot: Nov. 3-4 were found at Mount Mugh, about one hundred kilometres east of Samarkand.
spatial_interpretation.rule: Keep probable contract setting and later document findspot distinct; neither is a Sogdiana territorial-practice extent.

chronology_qualification.immutable_release_date_text: tenth regnal year of Tarkhun, king of Samarkand (ca. 709-710 CE)
chronology_qualification.later_catalogue_reference: Oxford Invisible East catalogue, citing Livshits 2015, lists Nov. 3/4 as 27 April 711.
chronology_qualification.rule: Do not silently rewrite the immutable released claim interval. The catalogue is not added as a new historical claim-source relation in this geometry tranche.

review_resolution.rationale: The mapped object is UNESCO WHC component 603rev-001, the Afrosiab Archaeological Area / ancient Samarkand. Existing Atlas precedent classifies authoritative UNESCO component site points as specialist geometry; uncertainty about whether this was the contract setting is carried by the claim-locus role, not by relabelling the component locator as a territorial extent.

new_locus_entity.display_name: Afrosiab (ancient Samarkand; probable Sogdian contract setting)
new_locus_entity.notes: Historical-city/archaeological-site context for the specialist-inferred probable place of contract conclusion. Not the Mount Mugh findspot, not an exact building/room, and not a Sogdiana practice extent.

geometry.resolution_method: Use UNESCO World Heritage component 603rev-001 as an authoritative representative locator for Afrosiab, ancient Samarkand. The point anchors the probable Samarkand legal context inferred by the specialist editor; it is not an exact contract site, not the Mount Mugh findspot, and not a territorial-practice polygon.

geometry_source.temporal_scope: Modern authoritative component locator for the enduring archaeological area of ancient Samarkand
geometry_source.independence_notes: Geometry-only authority; independent of the historical slavery/status classification.
geometry_source.reliability_limitations: The UNESCO component coordinate locates the 229 ha Afrosiab Archaeological Area. It does not identify the exact contract building or room and does not define Sogdiana territorial-practice extent.
